jobs.description:
Job Posting: Los Banos Nutria Operations Supervisor

Department of Fish and Wildlife

JC-538960



Los Banos Nutria Operations Supervisor
  
SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)

$10,854.00 - $13,493.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **11/30/2026**

### **Job Description and Duties**

Under the supervision of the Wildlife and Lands Program Manager and direction of the Nutria Eradication Program Manager, the incumbent will serve as the an Operations Supervisor for the Nutria Eradication Program and the Central Region, supervising implementation of the nutria eradication efforts around the Los Banos portion of the nutria infestation. Duties include hiring, training, developing, providing technical guidance to, and supervising Environmental Scientists, Fish and Wildlife Technicians, and Scientific Aides to conduct nutria surveys, data collection, trapping, dispatching, necropsies, and other associated tasks in accordance with project protocols and the overall nutria eradication strategy. The Operations Supervisor will operate in close coordination with the 3 other Nutria Eradication Operations Supervisors, the project Planning Specialist, and field crew leads to ensure effective and cohesive implementation of the eradication strategy, and is responsible for communicating operational needs to the Nutria Eradication Program Manager and GIS Analyst.

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:

  

Personal Leave Program - Human Resources - CalHR.

Link to Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory) Exam: *CalCareers*

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

The nature of this position requires periodic travel between project offices in Los Banos, Fresno, Stockton, Fairfield, and Sacramento.

Work is both in an office and in the field. Must be able to work outside in extreme temperatures, walk on uneven terrain, deal with mosquitoes, ticks, and other stinging/biting insects, rattlesnakes and other wildlife. This position may require working weekends, holidays, atypical hours, and outdoors during adverse weather. Must attend meetings and work with staff throughout the State, including some daily and overnight travel.

  
  

The primary geographical focus of staff under this position will be in Merced, Stanislaus, Fresno, and Mariposa counties, but work may be assigned in any part of the area of nutria infestation.

  

### **Position Details**

**Job Code #:**

JC-538960

**Position #(s):**

565-481-0764-005

**Working Title:**

**Los Banos Nutria Operations Supervisor**

**Classification:**

SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SUPERVISORY)

$10,854.00 - $13,493.00

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**# of Positions:**

1

**Work Location:**

Merced County

**Telework:**

In Office

**Job Type:**

Permanent, Full Time

### **Department Information**

Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) employees are committed to managing and protecting California’s diverse wildlife and the habitats upon which they depend.

  
  

California is one of the most biodiverse places on the planet. As such, CDFW values diverse employees working together to protect nature for all Californians. CDFW is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment where all backgrounds, cultures and personal experiences can thrive and connect others to our critical mission.

  
  

Join us and begin a meaningful new career!

  

Department Website: https://www.wildlife.ca.gov

### **Special Requirements**

* Must be willing and able to competently use pellet pistols or firearms as per the Department’s Policy for Non-Enforcement Personnel.

* Must be willing and able to competently use and possess wildlife restraint drugs and equipment.

* Must be willing to handle live animals and carcasses, dispatch animals, and conduct simple tissue sampling and necropsies.

* Must be willing and able to obtain a California Boater Card and other motorboat operator certifications as determined necessary.

* Must be in good physical condition and able to lift up to 40 pounds.

* Must possess valid Driver's License and be able to safely and effectively operate watercraft and UTVs, as well as tow trailers.

* Must wear a Department uniform.

The selected candidate may be required to provide transcripts (may be unofficial).

### **Application Instructions**

Completed applications and all required documents must be received or postmarked by the Final Filing Date in order to be considered. Dates printed on Mobile Bar Codes, such as the Quick Response (QR) Codes available at the USPS, are not considered Postmark dates for the purpose of determining timely filing of an application.

Final Filing Date: 11/30/2026

Who May Apply

Individuals who are currently in the classification, eligible for lateral transfer, eligible for reinstatement, have list or LEAP eligibility, are in the process of obtaining list eligibility, or have SROA and/or Surplus eligibility (please attach your letter, if available). SROA and Surplus candidates are given priority; therefore, individuals with other eligibility may be considered in the event no SROA or Surplus candidates apply. Individuals who are eligible for a Training and Development assignment may also be considered for this position(s).

Job Posting: ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (00100762)

Department of Water Resources

JC-536356



ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (00100762)
  
ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST

$4,551.00 - $9,787.00 per Month
  
New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**Final Filing Date:** **12/7/2026**

### **Job Description and Duties**

The California Department of Water Resources (DWR) is seeking an Environmental Scientist to join our talented team of hydrographic science professionals in the Bathymetry Data Collection Section. This position is ideal for a dedicated professional who excels in dynamic outdoor field environments interested in operating sonar and other technical scientific data collection equipment, while possessing a strong analytical mindset for in-office data processing and analysis. The incumbent will be responsible for completing a variety of professional scientific duties as part of a Team involving the collection, processing, management, quality assurance/quality control (QA/QC), and analysis of bathymetric, hydrographic and other environmental and geographic information, generally within the Sacramento-San Joaquin River Delta and at facilities related to the State Water Project. The successful candidate will demonstrate a strong aptitude for boating and marine field work, experience operating advanced water science equipment including sonar technology, and a proactive approach to troubleshooting technical, mechanical, and electrical issues. In addition, the candidate will possess a keen interest in office based data processing, data investigations, spatial analysis and ability to prepare related exhibits and presentations using ArcGIS, CARIS, PowerPoint and related software.

At DWR, you will have the advantage of numerous resources to support your work and your professional growth, including training opportunities, state-of-the-art software applications and tools, and knowledgeable and professional colleagues to assist with project success. As an employee of DWR, your work is critical in the delivery of water to over 26 million Californians, as well as contributing to protecting our environment. We hope you’ll review the Duties and Desirable Qualifications below and apply for this great career opportunity to join our team.

  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

**Job Code #:**

JC-536356

**Position #(s):**

846-300-0762-010

**Working Title:**

**Classification:**

$4,551.00 - $6,337.00 A

$5,531.00 - $7,718.00 B

$7,000.00 - $9,787.00 C

New to State candidates will be hired into the minimum salary of the classification or minimum of alternate range when applicable.

**# of Positions:**

1

**Work Location:**

Yolo County

**Telework:**

In Office

**Job Type:**

Permanent, Full Time

### **Department Information**

**Division of Regional Assistance, North Central Region Office, Resources Assessment Branch/Bathymetry Data Collection Section, West Sacramento**

Department of Water Resources (DWR) was established in 1956 by the California State Legislature. We manage California’s water resources, systems, and infrastructure, including the State Water Project, in a responsible sustainable way.

At DWR, we are embedding climate change response into every project we undertake. We have set standards to help evaluate how each project incorporates climate resilience principles and ensure consistency across the Department. Our mission is to sustainably manage the water resources of California, in cooperation with other agencies, to benefit the state’s people and protect, restore, and enhance the natural and human environments.

DWR also strives to create a trusting and welcoming workplace where employees embrace diverse viewpoints and treat each other with civility and respect. An important component of DWR’s equal employment opportunity program centers around justice, equity, diversity, and inclusion.

Department Website: https://water.ca.gov/

Free virtual career consultation services including one-on-one DWR career consultations, application/resume review, tips for applying, and mock interviews, provided by DWR’s Recruitment and Workforce Planning section can now be scheduled via https://water.ca.gov/About/Careers.

### **Special Requirements**

Possession of a valid California driver license is required. Possessing or obtaining a California Boater Card will also be required. The fieldwork described above will require driving and walking on public and private roadways and on uneven terrain and the ability to bend, stoop, twist, traverse and lift loads up to approximately 50 pounds. Candidates should be able to work on and around swift moving waterways.

  

All employees are responsible for contributing to an inclusive, safe, and secure work environment that values diverse cultures, perspectives, and experiences, and is free from discrimination.

### **Application Instructions**

Completed applications and all required documents must be received or postmarked by the Final Filing Date in order to be considered. Dates printed on Mobile Bar Codes, such as the Quick Response (QR) Codes available at the USPS, are not considered Postmark dates for the purpose of determining timely filing of an application.

Final Filing Date: 12/7/2026

Who May Apply

Individuals who are currently in the classification, eligible for lateral transfer, eligible for reinstatement, have list or LEAP eligibility, are in the process of obtaining list eligibility, or have SROA and/or Surplus eligibility (please attach your letter, if available). SROA and Surplus candidates are given priority; therefore, individuals with other eligibility may be considered in the event no SROA or Surplus candidates apply.

jobs.title: Safety & Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
**THE JOB**

Tidewater Barge Lines is looking for a QHSSE Specialist to join our team to support our shipyard and environmental services teams! In this role, you will support the Company’s Quality, Health, Safety, Security, and Environmental programs by ensuring regulatory compliance, managing risk, and promoting a strong safety culture across facilities and operations, with an emphasis on shipyard and environmental services operations. This role conducts audits, inspections, and investigations. You’ll lead trainings and perform industrial hygiene assessments while providing guidance on QHSSE policies, procedures, and best practices. The position partners with employees and management to drive continuous improvement in safety performance, compliance, operational excellence, and environmental stewardship.

***Position will remain open until sufficient applicants are received***

The QHSSE Specialist responsibilities span multiple areas:

* **Safety Leadership & Risk Management**

  + Promotes and supports safe, incident-free operations and demonstrates compliance with applicable safety management system policies, procedures, and expectations. While providing technical expertise in the anticipation, recognition, assessment, and mitigation of risk
  + Administers Behavior-Based Safety (BBS) programs for the Shipyard and Environmental Services operations, including data analysis, hazard and risk assessment, corrective actions, and employee engagement.
  + Conducts industrial hygiene assessments and exposure monitoring, including air quality, noise, chemical, and other occupational exposures. Maintains, calibrates, and supports the proper use of applicable monitoring and testing equipment.
  + Analyzes safety, incident, exposure, and environmental data to recommend improvements to policies, and procedures while leading incident investigations, root cause analyses, and the development, implementation, and follow-up of corrective and preventive action processes.

* **Regulatory Compliance & Environmental Stewardship**

  + Monitors and supports compliance with applicable federal, state, and local safety, environmental, occupational health, and security requirements, as well as company policies, standards, and industry best practices.
  + Maintains current knowledge of applicable QHSSE laws, regulations, standards, and industry best practices, and evaluates their impact on company operations.
  + Conducts inspections, audits, assessments, and other compliance-monitoring activities; identifies deficiencies, recommends corrective actions, and supports continuous improvement efforts.
  + Maintains accurate and timely regulatory and company-required records, documentation, and reports.
  + Provides field-level support to the Environmental Manager for environmental compliance activities, projects, inspections, and other environmental matters within assigned operational areas.
* **Training & Employee Engagement**

  + Administers QHSSE training programs, including training requirements, scheduling, recordkeeping, learning management system administration, compliance tracking, and execute QHSSE-related training and awareness programs.
  + Maintains an active field presence at Shipyard and Environmental Services work sites, including the facilitation of safety committee meetings to identify hazards, reinforce safe work practices, and support regulatory compliance.

* **Operational Support & Program Administration**

  + Utilize feedback to plan and coordinates QHSSE projects arising from safety committee activities, employee safety suggestions, audits, investigations, and regulatory requirements.
  + Provide safety equipment, personal protective equipment, supplies, monitoring equipment, and other QHSSE resources for assigned operational areas.
  + Supports company drug and alcohol testing programs by serving as a qualified/certified collector adhering to DOT company requirements.
  + Communicates significant compliance issues to appropriate leadership and track corrective actions through completion.

* **Field Operations & Site Support**

  + Travels to company facilities and vessels to conduct inspections, audits, investigations, training, compliance reviews, and other program support activities.
  + Partners with operational leaders, vessel crews, and shoreside employees to implement QHSSE initiatives and support continuous improvement.

**PAY & BENEFITS**

* Position hiring range: $80,000 – $90,000 (depending on experience and qualifications)
* Bonus Potential

* Healthcare benefits including medical, vision, dental, and prescriptions with low deductibles and copays. Company pays 91% of premiums for the employee and family
* Flexible Spending Account
* 401(k) with 6% company match
* 3% Profit Sharing Plan
* Sick and vacation accrued per paycheck
* Nine paid holidays and one floating holiday
* Educational Assistance Program

**THE CATCH**

* Associate or bachelor’s degree in environmental, health, safety and/or security or other related field of study, or an equivalent combination of relevant experience and education.
* One to three years’ experience with a focus on quality, health, safety, security, and environmental compliance required. Experience in industrial, marine, terminal, and/or shipyard setting preferred.
* Basic understanding and ability to interpret federal, state, and/or local safety and environmental codes, rules, regulations, and procedures.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to deliver safety and environmental training, collaborate effectively, resolve problems, influence change, and build productive relationships at all levels of the organization.
* Be available on an on-call basis nights, weekends, and holidays to help respond to emergency situations.
* Be able to travel regularly to company facilities and work sites, including shipyard, terminal, and other operational locations including Pasco, WA and Kent, WA.
* Use all required personal protective
